reader_conclusion: The 26-student randomized study supports better blinded OSCE performance, including transfer to new scenarios, in this course/cohort; broad curricular or real-clinical effectiveness remains a larger inference.

claims.content: Three weeks after the course, randomized e-course students scored higher than controls on the blinded evaluation (59.3±6.2 vs 41.8±10.2; p=0.0020).

evidence_relations.reason: The randomized blinded post-course assessment directly reports the overall score difference.

support.reason: The bounded claim preserves the 26-student sample, short follow-up, and simulated assessment endpoint.

claims.content: The e-course group also outperformed controls on course-related items (about 1.7-fold; p=0.0034) and on new clinical scenarios (about 1.3-fold; p=0.0098).

evidence_relations.reason: The prespecified subscale comparisons directly support both near-content learning and transfer to novel simulated scenarios.

support.source_location: Abstract/Results: prespecified content and new-scenario subscales
support.reason: The source directly reports significant performance differences on both subscales.

claims.content: The course broadly improves medical students' real clinical imaging-ordering and downstream decision-making across curricula and institutions.

evidence_relations.reason: The overall blinded assessment supports learning in the enrolled cohort.
Novel simulated scenarios support near transfer, but not real-patient behavior or other curricula/institutions.

support.reason: The trial has only 26 students, one course and institution context, a three-week follow-up, and simulated/OSCE outcomes rather than observed clinical practice.

author_boundary.summary: The authors acknowledge the small sample, single educational context, short follow-up, and simulated assessment setting, and call for broader validation before general curricular or clinical conclusions.
author_boundary.source_location: Discussion/Conclusion; study limitations and future validation

reasoning_edges.added_reach: Uses randomized access to the course and blinded assessment to attribute the bounded score difference to the e-course in this cohort.
assumptions: Randomization and blinded evaluation preserve the intended treatment contrast despite the small sample.

reasoning_edges.added_reach: Attributes the bounded subscale differences to randomized course access in the studied cohort.
assumptions: The prespecified subscales validly measure course-related performance and near transfer to new simulated scenarios.

reasoning_edges.added_reach: Extends short-term simulated assessment gains in 26 students to real clinical behavior and broad curricular transfer.
assumptions: OSCE/new-scenario performance predicts durable real-patient decisions and transfers across institutions and curricula.

usable.results: The randomized overall and subscale assessment differences are directly useful for this course/cohort.
usable.methods_or_design: Blinded evaluation with both trained-content and new-scenario subscales is a useful transfer-sensitive education design.
usable.materials_or_documentation: Randomization, cohort size, course structure, assessment timing, endpoints, and p-values are reported.

downweight.worth_noticing: The new-scenario subscale provides stronger evidence than testing only memorized course content.
downweight.cautious_or_ignore: Do not equate a small short-term simulated educational outcome with demonstrated real clinical behavior.

uncertainty_and_follow_up: Larger multicenter cohorts, longer retention, and real/simulated clinical behavior endpoints would test durability and transfer.
